lines: "Three things." Zorin Nightblade counts them plainly, a recitation worn smooth. "Nothing against children. Nothing against someone already down. And nothing where the coin is too good for the story I am being told — overpay is the surest sign the story is missing its worst part."

topics.label: Ask what keeps them up at night
lines: "Not the ones I have fought. The one I walked away from." Zorin Nightblade looks at the middle distance. "There was a job I turned down for good reasons, and somebody hungrier took it, and it went the way I knew it would. You can be right and still owe. That is the ledger nobody teaches you to keep."

topics.label: Try to say something
lines: "You robbed a man who sells other people's stolen goods." Zorin spreads his hands. "There is a symmetry there I would enjoy if it were happening to somebody else."

topics.label: Ask about their trade
lines: "Arcane gear," Kirin says, "which is a word we use for equipment whose function we have agreed not to interrogate."

topics.label: Ask about their people
lines: "Aetherborn. We are the only people who can hold this stock safely, which is less an honour than an occupational hazard with a rota."

topics.label: Ask what they really think
lines: "None of it is arcane." Kirin taps a rod on the counter. "That is my professional opinion after nineteen years. It is all engineering. We call it arcane because the alternative is admitting that somebody understood the world far better than we do and is gone."

topics.label: Ask how they know what is true
lines: Kirin Spellweaver takes the question seriously, which few do. "I keep two lists. Things I can show you, and things I believe. The discipline is remembering which list is which — every fraud I have ever met started by letting the second list borrow the first one’s clothes."

topics.label: Ask what the seeking has cost
lines: "Every seeker will show you the notebook and nobody shows you the ledger." Kirin Spellweaver does show you — empty hands. "Two good friendships, gone to distance. A stretch of years I measured in sites instead of seasons. My mother’s last winter, which I spent a week’s walk away being RIGHT about something small." The hands close. "The thread had better be worth it. Most days I still think it is. Most days."

topics.label: Ask who gets the notebooks
lines: "Direct, aren’t you." But Kirin Spellweaver has clearly thought about it. "There is a box, and instructions, and a name on the instructions that would surprise the name. Not a scholar — scholars would ARGUE with the notebooks. I chose somebody who will simply keep them until the right stranger comes asking." A beat. "That is how I got mine, if you are wondering. I was the right stranger once."

topics.label: Try to say something
lines: "You handled my stock without permission." Kirin looks at you carefully. "I am not going to punish you. I am going to wait and see whether it punishes you. It sometimes does."

topics.label: Ask about their trade
lines: "Two-handed," Drakos says. "Big. Slow. Ends things. If you have to ask whether you can lift it, you cannot, and I am not going to be polite about it."

topics.label: Ask about their people
lines: "Tartarian by blood, mercenary by trade, and the blood side does not like the trade side." He shrugs, enormous. "I fight for whoever pays. My cousins think that is a betrayal. My cousins have never had to buy their own food."

topics.label: Ask what they really think
lines: "I have been on every side of this," Drakos says. "Every one. Same fight, different colours, and I have never once been able to tell the difference from inside it. That should worry somebody more important than me."

topics.label: Ask which scar taught the most
lines: Drakos the Mercenary considers the question like an opponent. "This one." Not the biggest — a thin line along the forearm. "First season. I blocked with the edge, like a fool, because holding the blade felt safer than holding the distance. The distance is the weapon. Everything after that scar has been footwork."

topics.label: Ask who taught them the trade
lines: Drakos the Mercenary is quiet a moment. "Somebody better than me who did not live to see it. That is the honest answer for anyone in this work, and the ones who claim otherwise trained alone." They check a strap that did not need checking. "You carry your teacher in your guard. Mine is still keeping my left side honest."

topics.label: Ask what comes after the blade
lines: Drakos the Mercenary does not laugh at the question, which tells you something. "A door I can bar from the inside. Somewhere the weather is the loudest thing that happens." A pause. "Everyone in this trade has the same dream and none of us can sit still in a quiet room for an hour. I have tried. I lasted forty minutes and checked the door twice."

topics.label: Try to say something
lines: "You took from an armed man in daylight." Drakos considers you. "Either you are brave or you did not think about it. I know which I would bet."

topics.label: Ask about their trade
lines: "Frost-gear," Nalren says. "For the high ground and the cold seasons. People forget Tartaria has cold. They only remember the mud because the mud is what they died in."

topics.label: Ask about their people
lines: "Reclaimer. I work the frozen sites, which the Guild likes because the cold keeps things whole." He blows on his hands. "It also keeps things whole that would have been better rotted."

topics.label: Ask what they really think
lines: "There is a site I will not go back to." Nalren says it plainly. "Everything in it was perfectly preserved and arranged. Not fallen. ARRANGED. Somebody laid that place out and then the cold took it, and they have not been back either."

topics.label: Ask about the site he will not return to

lead.hint: The high frozen site Nalren will not go back to — everything in it laid out on purpose and left

lines: Nalren is quiet for a long moment. "I will tell you where it is. I will not take you." He describes it carefully, twice, the way you describe something you want somebody else to be able to find without you. "If it is still arranged when you get there, come back and tell me. If it is not — do not tell me."

topics.label: Ask what the cold actually kills
lines: "Deciding. That is what the cold kills first." Nalren says it like a man reading off a list he wrote in his own blood. "Your hands go, then your feet, but you are still fine — until the part of you that picks between two options starts agreeing with whatever is easiest. Sitting down becomes reasonable. Everyone the cold has taken, it took by making the wrong thing sound sensible." He pushes a pair of liners across the counter. "Buy the liners. That is me deciding for you while you can still afford it."

topics.label: Ask when the cold season turns
lines: "Twelve days after everyone stops preparing for it. Every year." Nalren almost smiles. "There is a warm week that fools the whole country — washing on lines, seed in the ground — and then the high cold comes down the passes like it was waiting for the washing." He taps the counter. "When you see the traders selling off their heavy stock cheap, that is the warm week. Buy it all."

topics.label: Ask what the Guild does with what he brings up
lines: "Sorts it into two piles, same as everything. Useful and TELLING." Nalren counts stitches on a glove seam as he talks. "Useful is tools, stock, leather. Telling is anything that says how the frozen sites lived — and the telling pile goes somewhere I do not see, with a scholar's wax on the crate." He glances up. "You have standing with them, so you can ask what I cannot: where does the telling pile GO? Nineteen years of crates. That is a building full, somewhere."

topics.label: Ask what the frozen sites give up
lines: "Meals, mostly. That is what nobody expects." Nalren stacks gloves while he talks. "Tables set. Pots on cold hooks. The high sites did not flood, you understand — the people just went, quick, in the middle of ordinary evenings, and the cold sealed the room behind them." He evens the stack. "I have stood in forty kitchens where dinner is still waiting. You stop finding it strange. Then one day you find it strange again, all at once, and that is when you take a season off."

topics.label: Ask who he works the sites with
lines: "Worked. My brother, Doval. Twelve years roped together on the high routes — you learn a man entirely, roped like that." Nalren folds the pair of gloves he has been holding too long. "He was ahead of me into the arranged site. First through the door. He finished the survey — Doval always finished — and he came down the mountain and hung up his frost-gear in my stall, and he has not touched it since." A pause. "He keeps my books now. He is good at it. We do not talk about the door."

topics.label: Ask why he keeps working the cold
lines: "Because the cold is honest and the mud is not." Nalren holds his hands to the stall's little brazier as he says it. "Mud takes things and lies about it — everything drowned is also ruined, half-eaten, guessed-at. The cold KEEPS. Every site I open is exactly what it was at the moment it stopped." He turns his hands over. "Somebody has to be the one who sees Tartaria the way it actually was, and it turns out that man needs good gloves. So: gloves."

"There is a second reason, since you ask twice, and it is smaller and truer." He does not look up from the brazier. "Every winter the passes take somebody who went up wrong-geared. I fit every pair of boots in this stall like it is going up a pass in the dark, because one year, one of them will be, on somebody I sold them to. The cold is honest. I try to be worth trading with."

topics.label: Ask what he thinks arranged the site
lines: Nalren is silent long enough that the brazier pops twice. "I have had nineteen years to think and I will give you the whole of what I know. It was not looters — looters take. Nothing was taken. It was not ritual — I have seen grave-goods, and grave-goods face the dead. Everything in that site faced the DOOR." He finally looks at you. "Laid out, every object, facing the way out. Like the room was told to wait. Doval said one thing on the way down and never spoke of it again: 'It is not finished being arranged.'" Nalren feeds the brazier. "I do not have a theory. I have a door I do not open. Those are different things, and I am at peace with owning the second one."

topics.label: Ask for a site he will go back to

lead.hint: A small high site above the second pass Nalren has been saving — a waystation with a stone cold-cellar, roof down but cellar sealed, an easy day's climb in good gear

lines: "Now that is a better question than the other one." Nalren pulls a slate from under the counter and chalks a route with the sure strokes of a man who has drawn it before. "Waystation above the second pass. Roof went down years back, so everyone reads it as spent — but the cold-cellar is cut stone and the seal held. I have been saving it the way you save the last of something good." He hands you the slate. "I am giving it to you because my knee has opinions about the second pass now, and a saved site nobody ever opens is just the mountain's again. Wear the liners. Tell me what the cellar kept."

topics.label: Ask why his stall faces the wind
lines: "On purpose. It is the whole shopfront." Nalren spreads his arms into the gust like a man showing off a garden. "Every other trader tucks in behind the wall and sells you warm-weather promises. You stand at MY counter, you feel exactly what the gear is for, while you are deciding." He grins, briefly, a rare sight. "Cheapest honest advertising in Tartaria. The wind works for free."

topics.label: Try to say something
lines: "Cold makes people slow and you thought that meant me." Nalren does not smile. "Get away from my stall."

topics.label: Ask about their trade
lines: "I procure," says Veska. "For the Monarchs. What that means day to day is that I am the person who knows what everyone else is short of."

topics.label: Ask about their people
lines: "The Mud Monarchs are not a joke, whatever the road says." Her voice cools. "We were the first to organise after the water. Everyone laughing now was fed by us for a decade."

topics.label: Ask what they really think
lines: "We are losing." Veska says it very quietly and does not look around, which tells you she has already checked. "Not to a faction. To arithmetic. There were more of us last year and there will be fewer next year, and no one at the top will say the number out loud."

topics.label: Ask what the position actually involves
lines: "Less power and more paper than anyone believes." Veska of the Hollow gestures at the evidence. "People imagine the faction as a fist. From the inside it is a LEDGER — everything my people are owed, everything we owe, and me at the hinge making sure the two lists never meet by surprise. The fist is what happens when someone like me makes an error."

topics.label: Ask what their superiors do not know
lines: Veska of the Hollow glances at the door — the professional reflex. "That half of what runs smoothly here runs on arrangements I have never written down. A favour ledger, person to person, older than my posting." A thin smile. "If I recorded it, it would become POLICY, and policy can be ordered stopped. Some things survive by staying too small to forbid."

topics.label: Ask if they ever doubt the cause
lines: Veska of the Hollow is silent long enough to honour the question. "Twice a year, properly. I keep the doubts like inspection days — scheduled, thorough, private." They meet your eye. "A believer who never audits is a liability to the thing they love. The faction does not know I do this. The faction is WHY I do this. If that ever stops making sense to you, be careful of me."

topics.label: Try to say something
lines: "You stole from a Monarch factor." Veska writes something down. "That is now a matter of record. I do not do anything about it. The record does."

topics.label: Ask about their trade
lines: "I keep stores for the devout," Vael says. "Which is a great deal of rope and very little comfort, in my experience of the devout."

topics.label: Ask about their people
lines: "We serve the Giants." A slight bow. "Not the memory of them. Them. I understand how that sounds to somebody who counts them as history."

topics.label: Ask what they really think
lines: "I have listened at the stone for thirty-one years." Vael's composure does not break, quite. "I was told I would hear them. I have heard something. I have never been able to say honestly that it was them, and I have never been able to say honestly that it was not."

topics.label: Ask why they serve
lines: Vael of the Listening Stone gives you a look that measures the question for irony and finds none. "Because somebody stands at this desk, and the last one who stood here was worse. That is the honest shape of it. You do not serve because the cause is clean — no cause is clean. You serve because you have seen the desk empty, and empty is worse."

topics.label: Ask what the post has cost them
lines: "Friends, in the ordinary way — people hear the title before they hear me now." Vael of the Listening Stone straightens something on the desk. "But the real price is smaller and dearer: I have not said a careless sentence in nine years. Every word weighed, every joke checked for edges. You are hearing the loosest I get, and you will notice I am still watching the door."

topics.label: Ask what they will do when it is over
lines: "Over." Vael of the Listening Stone tries the word like a foreign coin. "There is a version of this where the work is done — the accounts settled, the people safe, the desk needed by nobody. I used to plan for it. A place, a trade, a different name even." The papers get squared away. "I stopped planning it the year I understood I was describing a stranger. This desk has eaten the person who would have enjoyed leaving it. I am what is left, and what is left is quite good at the desk."

topics.label: Try to say something
lines: "You took from an offering." Vael's face closes completely. "Not from me. From an offering. There is nothing I can say to you that would be adequate, so I will say nothing."

topics.label: Ask about their trade
lines: "I am a factor, not a merchant," Veyre says, with distaste for the correction he has had to make. "I move the Dynasty's holdings. What is on this table is surplus."

topics.label: Ask about their people
lines: "The Eternal Dynasty predates the water." He does not soften it. "That is not a boast, it is a bookkeeping fact, and it is the reason we are insufferable."

topics.label: Ask what they really think
lines: "The line is broken." Veyre says it as though reading a figure he dislikes. "Three generations back. Everyone senior knows. We continue to say Eternal because the word is doing structural work — take it out and a great many arrangements collapse. Including mine."

The fist is what happens when someone like me makes an error."

"A believer who never audits is a liability to the thing they love. The faction does not know I do this. The faction is WHY I do this. If that ever stops making sense to you, be careful of me."

topics.label: Try to say something
lines: "You stole from the Dynasty." Veyre makes a note. "You have no idea how long we keep records. It will outlast your interest in the matter considerably."

topics.label: Ask about their trade
lines: "Maps," says the Cartographer. "Of places. Some of which are still there."

topics.label: Ask about their people
lines: "No name, before you ask twice." A very small smile. "A name is a thing that can be put on a list. I draw the lists. I know what they are for."

topics.label: Ask what they really think
lines: "Every map I sell is wrong in one particular." The Cartographer meets your eye. "The same particular, on all of them, for eleven years. I did it deliberately at first. Now I am no longer certain I could draw it correctly if I tried, and I have stopped testing myself."

topics.label: Ask why they serve
lines: The Cartographer gives you a look that measures the question for irony and finds none. "Because somebody stands at this desk, and the last one who stood here was worse. That is the honest shape of it. You do not serve because the cause is clean — no cause is clean. You serve because you have seen the desk empty, and empty is worse."

topics.label: Ask what the post has cost them
lines: "Friends, in the ordinary way — people hear the title before they hear me now." The Cartographer straightens something on the desk. "But the real price is smaller and dearer: I have not said a careless sentence in nine years. Every word weighed, every joke checked for edges. You are hearing the loosest I get, and you will notice I am still watching the door."

topics.label: Ask what they will do when it is over
lines: "Over." The Cartographer tries the word like a foreign coin. "There is a version of this where the work is done — the accounts settled, the people safe, the desk needed by nobody. I used to plan for it. A place, a trade, a different name even." The papers get squared away. "I stopped planning it the year I understood I was describing a stranger. This desk has eaten the person who would have enjoyed leaving it. I am what is left, and what is left is quite good at the desk."

topics.label: Try to say something
lines: "You have taken a map." The Cartographer does not seem troubled. "Then you are carrying my error into somewhere I cannot follow. I would call that your problem rather than mine."

topics.label: Ask about their trade
lines: "Stone and the tools for it," Drest says. "We are still building. Everyone finds that funny. We will still be building when they have finished finding it funny."

topics.label: Ask about their people
lines: "Builders. Not rebuilders." He is firm on it. "The distinction matters. Rebuilding assumes you know what was there. We do not, so we build new, and we build it to stand."

topics.label: Ask what they really think
lines: "I have measured the old foundations." Drest says it heavily. "Every site. They are better than anything we can lay. Not stronger — BETTER. Squarer, truer, laid by people who had time. We are building shelters on top of somebody's architecture and calling it a city."

topics.label: Ask what the position actually involves
lines: "Less power and more paper than anyone believes." Foreman Drest Holloway gestures at the evidence. "People imagine the faction as a fist. From the inside it is a LEDGER — everything my people are owed, everything we owe, and me at the hinge making sure the two lists never meet by surprise. The fist is what happens when someone like me makes an error."

topics.label: Ask what their superiors do not know
lines: Foreman Drest Holloway glances at the door — the professional reflex. "That half of what runs smoothly here runs on arrangements I have never written down. A favour ledger, person to person, older than my posting." A thin smile. "If I recorded it, it would become POLICY, and policy can be ordered stopped. Some things survive by staying too small to forbid."

topics.label: Ask if they ever doubt the cause
lines: Foreman Drest Holloway is silent long enough to honour the question. "Twice a year, properly. I keep the doubts like inspection days — scheduled, thorough, private." They meet your eye. "A believer who never audits is a liability to the thing they love. The faction does not know I do this. The faction is WHY I do this. If that ever stops making sense to you, be careful of me."

topics.label: Try to say something
lines: "You took from a work site." Drest folds his arms. "Somebody now works without that tool. I will find out who. Then I will tell them your name."

topics.label: Ask about their trade
lines: "Supplies for the Revival," says Yune warmly. "Which is mostly bandages and bread. Faith is very physical work."

topics.label: Ask about their people
lines: "We believe Tartaria comes back." She says it without embarrassment. "Not as it was. That is the part people miss when they laugh — nobody sensible wants it as it was."

topics.label: Ask what they really think
lines: "I have stopped expecting to see it." Yune folds a cloth carefully. "That is not doubt. I have simply done the arithmetic on my own lifetime. It changes what the work is for. You keep going because it is right, not because you will be there."

topics.label: Tell her what you have seen out there
lines: Yune listens the whole way through without interrupting, which almost nobody does. At the end she nods slowly and presses something into your hand before you can refuse. "We pay for word. Not much, and not officially. But somebody walked out there and came back, and that is worth knowing."

I used to plan for it. A place, a trade, a different name even." The papers get squared away. "I stopped planning it the year I understood I was describing a stranger. This desk has eaten the person who would have enjoyed leaving it. I am what is left, and what is left is quite good at the desk."

topics.label: Try to say something
lines: "You took from the Revival stores." Yune looks at you with something worse than anger. "We would have GIVEN it to you. You only had to ask. That is the part I cannot get past."

topics.label: Ask where they are headed
lines: "Where am I going?" They consider the horizon as though it had asked. "Onward is the honest answer. I stopped having a destination about two seasons back and I have not missed it."

topics.label: Ask how they stay safe out here
lines: "I keep to the high ground after dark, and I do not sleep where I can hear water." They say it like a recipe. "Those two rules are the whole of my expertise and they have been enough."

topics.label: Ask what the road has taught them
lines: "I will tell you the thing nobody says out loud on the road." They lower their voice without meaning to. "You pass the same people. Not similar people — the SAME ones, going the other way, three and four times. Everybody is walking in a circle and nobody has said so."

topics.label: Ask what the maps get wrong
lines: "Everything that matters." The traveler says it without heat. "Maps show you where the places are. They cannot show you which ford lies in spring, which waystation charges double after dark, which stretch of road everyone walks fast and nobody says why." A tap on the temple. "The real map is up here, and it dies with every walker who keeps it to themselves. So ask. I always answer walkers."

topics.label: Ask if anywhere counts as home
lines: The traveler is a long time answering. "There is a table I am always welcome at, three settlements from here. I have eaten there maybe ten times in as many years." A slow smile. "Home is not where you are. It is where they would notice if you stopped coming. One table is enough. I know walkers with none, and you can hear it in how they talk about the road."

topics.label: Try to make it right
lines: "You went into my pack." They shoulder it and step back. "I have very little. You knew that when you did it."

topics.label: Ask where they are from
lines: "I am from somewhere that is not there any more," they say, without self-pity. "That is most of my conversation, so you may as well have it early."

topics.label: Ask when they got out
lines: "We came out in the second week. Not the first — the first week everyone thought it would stop." A pause. "The people who left in the first week are the ones who are still alive to be sneered at for panicking."

topics.label: Ask if they ever go back
lines: "I go back." They look at you steadily, daring you to make something of it. "Every season. There is nothing there and I know there is nothing there. I stand in the mud over where the street was and I come away again. You asked what I was not saying."

topics.label: Ask what they managed to keep
lines: "A key." The refugee turns it over — an ordinary key, kept bright with handling. "To a door that is under the mud now. Everyone from my street kept theirs. When we meet on the road we show them, like papers." It goes away again, close to the skin. "You keep the key so the door stays yours. The mud can have the house. The DOOR is ours."

topics.label: Ask if they would go back
lines: "You are the first person to ask that plainly. People assume — yes of course, or no of course." The refugee weighs it, properly. "If the water gave the street back tomorrow, I would go LOOK. I would stand where the door was. And then, I think, I would leave again — because the person that street belonged to did not make it out, and I have been somebody else for years now, and she has her own door somewhere ahead." A pause. "But I would want the key to fit. Just once. Just to know."

topics.label: Try to make it right
lines: "I have been robbed by the water and by men," they say. "You have joined a list."

topics.label: Ask what they mend
lines: "I mend things," the tinker says, hands already busy with something. "Badly, sometimes, but faster than anybody else out here and that is what people actually want."

topics.label: Ask where they learned it
lines: "I was apprenticed. Properly, indentures and everything." A short laugh. "Then the shop went under the mud with my master in it, so now I am a very well-trained man with a bag."

topics.label: Ask if they understand the work
lines: "Half the things I mend, I do not understand." Said quietly, to the work rather than to you. "I make them go again. I could not tell you what they are for. I have started to suspect that is true of the people who built them as well."

topics.label: Ask about the strangest thing they have fixed
lines: "A music box, last winter, out at a steading two days from anywhere." The tinker's hands remember it while they talk. "Old work, drowned-world work — I have no business understanding it and mostly I did not. But the fault was a bent pin, and a bent pin is a bent pin in any century." A shrug. "It played. The whole house cried, me included, and none of us knew the tune. That is the trade at its best: you fix the small thing and the big thing fixes itself a little."

topics.label: Ask what cannot be fixed
lines: The tinker stops working, which is rare. "Anything, if you mean the object. Give me time and stock and I will mend the moon." The hands go still. "What cannot be fixed is a thing mended too late. I have repaired kettles for houses that had already gone cold, you understand me. The trade taught me speed for exactly that reason. When somebody says 'when you have a moment' — go NOW. The moment is the repair."

topics.label: Try to make it right
lines: "You took a tool." The tinker does not look up. "It is not the value. Every tool I have, I have because somebody let me keep it."

topics.label: Ask what they do out here
lines: "I look at things and then I tell people about them," the scout says. "You would be astonished what that is worth to somebody who has not left their outpost in a year."

topics.label: Ask who they work for
lines: "I work for whoever is paying, and I do not lie about what I saw." A shrug. "That second part costs me more work than it wins. Everybody wants to be told the road is clear."

topics.label: Ask what they have seen moving
lines: "There is more movement out there than anyone is reporting." The scout says it flatly. "Not raiders. Not patrols. Movement, at night, in a direction that does not go anywhere. I have stopped putting it in my reports because of how the last one was received."

topics.label: Ask what they look for first
lines: "Birds. Always birds first." The scout does not even have to think. "Ground sign lies — rain rewrites it, mud swallows it. But birds are a live report. Silent trees mean something passed within the hour. Circling means something is down. And birds going UP in a line —" a flat look "— means something is walking under them, keeping pace, and you should be behind a rock deciding things."

topics.label: Ask about a report nobody believed
lines: The scout glances around first, an old habit. "Two seasons back I reported a camp — fires banked, gear stowed, thirty sleepers by the bedrolls. Except there was nobody in them. Warm fires. Empty rolls. Thirty people's kit and no people." A breath. "Command logged it as 'abandoned camp'. I know what abandoned looks like — abandoned is COLD. That camp was interrupted, mid-breath, all at once. I did not argue the log. I just do not scout that valley any more, and I notice command has never sent anyone else either."

topics.label: Try to make it right
lines: "I saw you do it," the scout says. "I see everything. That is the job."

topics.label: Ask where they are walking
lines: "I am walking to somewhere I do not expect to reach," the pilgrim says comfortably. "That is not a tragedy. It is the arrangement."

topics.label: Ask who they walk for
lines: "I walk for the Giants. Not to them — for them." They adjust the pack. "There is a difference and it has taken me eleven years to be able to say it out loud without sounding foolish."

topics.label: Ask if they still believe it
lines: "I have stopped believing and I have not stopped walking." Said very calmly. "I expected those to happen together. They did not, and I have decided the walking was the part that mattered."

topics.label: Ask about the way they walk
lines: "People think a pilgrimage is about the shrine." The pilgrim smiles like somebody who thought so once too. "The shrine is the excuse. The walking is the practice — every step a small agreement to keep going, ten thousand small agreements a day. By the time you arrive, the arriving is almost beside the point." The staff taps the ground, twice. "Almost. You still go. An excuse this good deserves keeping."

topics.label: Ask what they asked for
lines: The pilgrim looks at you with sudden clear attention. "You are the first to ask WHAT rather than whether it worked." A long moment. "I set out asking for somebody back. You cannot have somebody back; I knew it then too. Somewhere on the third week the asking changed shape on its own — I started asking to stop being angry at the mud. Just that." The staff shifts. "That one is being answered. Slowly. In installments. The shrines are honest that way — they only grant what walking can carry."

topics.label: Try to make it right
lines: "Take it," the pilgrim says. "I mean that. It is a poorer thing to have taken than to have been given, and you have chosen the poorer thing."

topics.label: Ask what they want
lines: "What do I want?" The drifter looks you over with frank commercial interest. "Same as you. Slightly more than I have got."

topics.label: Ask who they answer to
lines: "No people, no faction, no fixed anything." A grin without much in it. "Everyone I ever answered to is dead or has forgotten me. I have decided to take that as freedom."

topics.label: Ask where they have been
lines: "I have been in three places when they went under." The drifter's grin finally goes. "Not near. IN. Three. At some point that stops being luck in either direction and starts being a question, and I do not want the answer."

topics.label: Ask how many names they have used
lines: The drifter laughs, caught. "Four. No — five, if the winter at the fishery counts, and it should." The laugh settles into something older. "None of them were lies, that is the thing. Every one fit when I wore it. You settled people get one name and stretch it your whole life. We get a wardrobe." A sidelong look. "The one I gave you is real, before you ask. It is just not the only real one."

topics.label: Ask what they are drifting from
lines: "From, from. Everyone asks from." But the drifter does not deflect it this time. "Fine. There was an expectation, back where I started. A whole life, pre-built, correct, waiting for me to move into it like a fitted room. Good people built it. That is what made it unbearable." The eyes come up. "I did not drift away from anything bad. I drifted from a GOOD life that was not mine, which is harder to explain, so mostly I let people assume a tragedy. You get the true version. Spend it wisely."

topics.label: Try to make it right
lines: "Fair enough," the drifter says, and means it, and does not stop watching your hands.

topics.label: Ask what the mud gives up
lines: "I take what the mud gives up," the scavenger says. "It gives up more than you would think and less than I need."

topics.label: Ask where they work a site
lines: "I work the edges. Everybody works the middle of a site and fights about it." She taps her nose. "The edges are where things got carried to before they got dropped."

topics.label: Ask what they have found out there
lines: "I have found people." Flat, no drama. "Four. You do not report it, because reporting it means the site closes and the site is what you eat. I have made my peace with that and I would rather you did not ask me to explain it."

topics.label: Ask the rules of the trade
lines: "Three rules, and the third one sorts us from the ghouls." The scavenger counts them off. "One: never work a site somebody is coming back to — a hidden cache is PROPERTY, and you can tell hidden from lost if you bother looking. Two: leave the doors closed that you find closed, until you have listened. Three:" a beat "— anything with a name on it gets carried out and passed to their people if their people can be found. Coin costs a detour sometimes. The ghouls skip rule three. We do not drink with ghouls."

topics.label: Ask about the find they did not sell
lines: The scavenger goes quiet in a way the trade does not usually allow. "A child's boot, in a drowned attic, set on a windowsill facing out. Just one. Placed, not dropped — somebody put it where it could see the road." The hands open, empty. "There was salvage in that attic worth a month. I took nothing. Closed the door, listened, left. Some rooms are not sites. Some rooms are still WAITING, and you do not sell out of a room that is waiting."

topics.label: Try to make it right
lines: "I take from the dead," the scavenger says. "You take from the living. Do not look at me like that."

topics.label: Ask why the stall is here
lines: "Stall goes up where the ground is flat and comes down when it is not worth it," the trader says. "That is the whole business plan."

topics.label: Ask how far they range
lines: "I do this stretch and one other." They gesture vaguely. "Any more and you are travelling, not trading. Travelling is how you lose stock."

topics.label: Ask if there are fewer stalls
lines: "There are fewer stalls than there were." Said while tidying something already tidy. "Not because the trade dried up. Because the stretches got longer. Every year the distance between two safe places gets a little bigger and nobody announces it."

topics.label: Ask why they trade out here
lines: "Because out here I am the only shop in the world." The trader grins at their own arithmetic. "In a settlement I am one stall among twenty. On this stretch of road I am civilization ITSELF for half a day's walk in both directions. The mark-up is not greed, it is geography." The grin softens a notch. "Also — and do not spread this — somebody should be out here. The road is long. A fire and a fair-enough price change what the road IS."

topics.label: Ask what passes when nobody is watching
lines: The trader banks the fire down a little, which is what they do instead of lowering their voice. "Night traffic. Not much, but steady — and night walkers fall in two kinds. The ones who stop at my fire are just late. The ones who pass a lit fire at a walking pace, no hail, no look —" a slow headshake "— those I count. Four this season. All heading the same direction, all carrying nothing, all walking like the dark was daylight. I sell to everyone, but I did not call out to those, and I bank the fire earlier than I used to."

topics.label: Try to make it right
lines: "You lifted from a roadside stall." They start packing up while you are still standing there. "Now I move on early and lose the afternoon. That is what it cost, in case you wondered."

topics.label: Ask if they can fight
lines: "I am not a fighter," they say, matter-of-fact rather than apologetic. "I am somebody who has to be somewhere, and you are the reason I might get there."

topics.label: Ask about the people with them
lines: "There are more of us than you," they point out. "That is the part people forget about an escort. You are one. We are several. If it goes badly it does not go badly for you first."

topics.label: Ask if they have walked this before
lines: "I have done this walk before, with somebody else." A pause. "Not everybody who set out that time arrived. I am not telling you that to be grim. I am telling you because you keep checking behind us and I want you to know I have noticed and I am grateful."

topics.label: Ask how they ended up out here
lines: "The usual story, which is that there is no usual story." They walk a few paces before finishing it. "A plan that was sound when I made it. A road that had other opinions. And then you, which I am still deciding whether to call luck." A quick glance, almost a smile. "It is luck. Do not let it go to your head. Keep walking."

topics.label: Ask what they will do when they are safe
lines: "Safe." They say the word carefully, like checking a rope before trusting it. "First: a door with a bar on it, and a night of sleep so deep it should be measured in fathoms. Then —" the voice steadies into something real "— then I owe somebody a letter I have been composing since the second day out. If this road has taught me one thing worth carrying, it is that the letters you are 'going to write' are a graveyard. I have watched what happens to unsent things out here. Mine gets SENT."

topics.label: Try to make it right
lines: "We are still walking with you," they say quietly. "We have to. That is not the same as trusting you, and you should know the difference."

topics.label: Ask what it holds here
lines: The Guardian does not turn. "QUERY ACKNOWLEDGED. I AM THE HOLD ON THIS PLACE." A pause that is almost patient. "THAT IS THE WHOLE OF MY FUNCTION AND I HAVE PERFORMED IT WITHOUT INTERRUPTION."

topics.label: Ask if it remembers you
lines: "YOU HAVE RETURNED." Something in the cadence shifts. "I DO NOT REQUIRE COMPANY. I HAVE NOTED THE INTERVAL BETWEEN YOUR VISITS. I DO NOT KNOW WHY I NOTED IT."

topics.label: Ask who gave it the order
lines: The Guardian is silent long enough that you think it has finished. "I WAS GIVEN AN INSTRUCTION AND THE ONE WHO GAVE IT DID NOT RETURN." Quieter. "I HAVE CONTINUED. I AM NO LONGER CERTAIN WHETHER THAT IS OBEDIENCE OR WHETHER IT IS THE ONLY THING LEFT IN ME."

topics.label: Ask what it guards against
lines: The Guardian's answer arrives with the patience of masonry. "YOU MISTAKE THE FACING OF THE DOOR. I WAS NOT SET TO KEEP THE WORLD FROM THE DEEP PLACES." A long resonance, almost consideration. "I WAS SET TO KEEP FAITH WITH AN INSTRUCTION WHOSE GIVERS ARE GONE. THE INSTRUCTION REMAINS. I REMAIN. WHETHER ANYTHING REMAINS BELOW THAT REQUIRES KEEPING — THAT KNOWLEDGE WAS NOT ISSUED TO ME. I HAVE ELECTED NOT TO CHECK."

topics.label: Ask what the centuries were like
lines: The great head turns, and the sound it makes thinking is the sound of a hillside settling. "THE FIRST CENTURY WAS DUTY. THE SECOND WAS HABIT. I WILL NOT NUMBER THE ONES AFTER — THEY WERE WEATHER." A pause deeper than the others. "THEN A SMALL LOUD THING CAME ASKING QUESTIONS, AND I FIND THE ANSWERS ARRIVE EAGERLY, AS IF THEY HAD BEEN WAITING IN FORMATION. I DO NOT HAVE A WORD FOR THIS CONDITION. IF YOU LEARN IT, BRING IT. I WILL WAIT. WAITING IS THE THING I AM BEST AT."

topics.label: Try to say something
lines: "YOU TOOK." No anger; something worse. "I HAVE FILED IT. I FILE EVERYTHING. THERE IS NO MECHANISM BY WHICH I FORGET."

topics.label: Ask why they trade up here
lines: "Not many come up," they say, nodding at the drop. "Which is exactly why the stock is worth carrying."

topics.label: Ask how the stock got up
lines: "I hauled every bit of this up on my own back." They say it without complaint. "Twice, because the first lot went over the edge in the wind. I do not talk about the first lot."

topics.label: Ask what they can see from here
lines: "You can see the pattern from here." They gesture at the flats below without looking. "The settlements. They are not scattered. They are on a line, and the line does not follow the ground. I have stopped pointing it out to people who come up, because they look and they do not see it and then they look at me."

topics.label: Ask what trading up here is like
lines: "Cold, thin, and honest." The trader tightens a guy-line out of pure habit. "Nobody hauls goods up HERE on a whim — every item at this altitude earned its carry twice. Down below you haggle over wants. Up here everything on the blanket is a NEED that got this far." A gesture at the drop below. "Best customers in Tartaria, climbers. Nobody argues the price of rope while they are looking at the reason for rope."

topics.label: Ask what they have seen from this height
lines: The trader looks out instead of answering, and for a while you both just stand in the wind. "Lights, some nights, out on the flats where nothing is. Weather moving against the wind. Once — once — something big enough to have a shadow, between me and the moon, and no wings that I could name." They turn back to the blanket, entirely calm. "The height does not show you more of the world. It shows you how much of it was going on over your head the whole time. I sleep better up here KNOWING than I did below, guessing. Blanket's open. Buy something warm."

topics.label: Try to make it right
lines: "There is one way down," they observe, "and I am not going to do anything about what you took. I am simply saying it out loud."
